messages.content:
The workspace contains `perf.py` — a module whose functions are CORRECT but
too slow for production. Your job: make every function fast enough to pass
the timing budgets below while keeping the results identical.

Functions and their required behavior (unchanged):

- `common_elements(a, b)` — sorted list of values appearing in both lists
- `fib(n)` — nth Fibonacci number (fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1)
- `count_pairs(nums, target)` — number of index pairs i<j with
  nums[i]+nums[j] == target
- `dedupe_keep_order(items)` — remove duplicates, preserving first-seen order

Timing budgets (generous — any reasonable algorithmic fix sails through):
- `common_elements` on two 200,000-element lists: under 2 seconds
- `fib(300)`: under 2 seconds
- `count_pairs` on 100,000 elements: under 2 seconds
- `dedupe_keep_order` on 200,000 items: under 2 seconds

Rules: keep the function names and signatures; standard library only; the
module must still import cleanly. Correctness is tested with exact expected
values — optimize the algorithms, don't approximate.

text:
All four functions are optimized and verified — every budget passes with huge margin, and results match the original algorithms exactly.

Changes in `perf.py` (names and signatures unchanged, stdlib only):

- **`common_elements`**: set intersection instead of nested list scans — 0.03s on two 200k lists (was O(n·m·k)).
- **`fib`**: iterative pair-swap instead of exponential recursion — fib(300) in effectively 0s, verified against the known 300th Fibonacci value.
- **`count_pairs`**: single pass with a complement-count dict (counts pairs against elements seen so far, so i<j ordering and duplicates are handled exactly) — 0.006s on 100k elements.
- **`dedupe_keep_order`**: membership check against a set instead of the output list — 0.003s on 200k items.

Correctness was verified by brute-force comparison against the original algorithms on 200 randomized small inputs per function (duplicates and negatives included), plus the fib(0..10) sequence and exact fib(300). The scratch verification script was removed afterward.
